```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
library(tidyverse)
library(maps)        
library(ggplot2)
library(mapproj)
library(ggthemes)
library(tidyquant)
library(readxl)
library(ggmap)
```

# 1. Generate a map of your home location 

```{r}
#getting ohio map
map.county <- map_data('county')  
ohio.county <- subset(map.county, region=="ohio")

#hometown coordinates
wapak_df <- data.frame(long=-84.19408, lat=40.56894)

#US map
states_map <- map_data("state")

#plot of my hometown
ggplot() +
  geom_polygon(data = states_map, aes(x=long,y=lat,group=group), fill="white", colour=
                 "black") +
  geom_point(data = wapak_df, aes(x = long, y = lat)) +
  annotate(geom="text",x=-84.19408,y=40.56894, label="Wapakoneta",adj=-0.05, color="red")+
  theme_nothing()
```

# 2. Generate a choropleth map of Ohio and shade counties by their case rate per thousand

```{r, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE}
#get corona cases from ohio.gov
ohioDF <- read_csv("https://coronavirus.ohio.gov/static/COVIDSummaryData.csv")
#get ohio population from census.gov source = https://www.census.gov/data/datasets/time-
#series/demo/popest/2010s-counties-total.html#par_textimage_739801612
ohioPop <- read_excel("co-est2019-annres-39.xlsx")

#get the date
Today <- Sys.Date()

#filter out row of totals and mutate variables
ohioDF <- ohioDF %>% 
  filter(Sex != "Total") %>% 
  mutate(OnsetDate = mdy(`Onset Date`)) %>% 
  filter(Today - OnsetDate <= 30) %>% 
  group_by(County) %>% 
  summarize(ncases = sum(`Case Count`))

#filter out unneeded rows and columns before combining tables
ohioPop <- ohioPop[c(-1, -2, -3, -4, -93, -94, -95, -96, -97),2]

#combine tables and changing variables
#rename county to region to map it with ohio.county
#https://www.sharpsightlabs.com/blog/rename-columns-in-r/
combinedOhio <- cbind(ohioDF, ohioPop) %>% 
  mutate(countyPop = as.double(`...2`)) %>% 
  select(!`...2`) %>% 
  mutate(rate = (ncases/countyPop) * 1000) %>% 
  mutate(County = str_to_lower(County)) %>% 
  rename(subregion = County)

#combine all data sets into one
rateDB <- merge(ohio.county, combinedOhio, by.x = "subregion", by.y = "subregion")
  
#map
ggplot(data = rateDB, aes(x=long,y=lat,group = group, fill=rate)) +
  geom_polygon(color = "black") +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low="#559999",mid="grey90",high="#BB650B",
                      midpoint=median(rateDB$rate)) +
  labs(title = "Ohio COVID-19 Infection Rates per 1000 Residents over the last 30 Days", 
       subtitle = paste("Updated: ", Today)) +
  theme_map() +
  theme(legend.position = "right")
```
